2158.name: chrono
2158.docs:
# Chrono: Date and Time for Rust

Chrono aims to provide all functionality needed to do correct operations on dates and times in
the [proleptic Gregorian calendar]:

245.name: prelude
245.docs: A convenience module appropriate for glob imports (`use chrono::prelude::*;`).

158.name: Date
158.docs:
ISO 8601 calendar date with time zone.

You almost certainly want to be using a [`NaiveDate`] instead of this type.

250.name: from_utc
250.docs:
Makes a new `Date` with given *UTC* date and offset.
The local date should be constructed via the `TimeZone` trait.

251.name: and_time
251.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date and given `NaiveTime`.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Returns `None` on invalid datetime.

252.name: and_hms
252.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute and second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Panics on invalid hour, minute and/or second.

253.name: and_hms_opt
253.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute and second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Returns `None` on invalid hour, minute and/or second.

254.name: and_hms_milli
254.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute, second and millisecond.
The millisecond part can exceed 1,000 in order to represent the leap second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Panics on invalid hour, minute, second and/or millisecond.

255.name: and_hms_milli_opt
255.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute, second and millisecond.
The millisecond part can exceed 1,000 in order to represent the leap second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Returns `None` on invalid hour, minute, second and/or millisecond.

256.name: and_hms_micro
256.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute, second and microsecond.
The microsecond part can exceed 1,000,000 in order to represent the leap second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Panics on invalid hour, minute, second and/or microsecond.

257.name: and_hms_micro_opt
257.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute, second and microsecond.
The microsecond part can exceed 1,000,000 in order to represent the leap second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Returns `None` on invalid hour, minute, second and/or microsecond.

258.name: and_hms_nano
258.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute, second and nanosecond.
The nanosecond part can exceed 1,000,000,000 in order to represent the leap second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Panics on invalid hour, minute, second and/or nanosecond.

259.name: and_hms_nano_opt
259.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from the current date, hour, minute, second and nanosecond.
The nanosecond part can exceed 1,000,000,000 in order to represent the leap second.
The offset in the current date is preserved.

Returns `None` on invalid hour, minute, second and/or nanosecond.

260.name: succ
260.docs:
Makes a new `Date` for the next date.

Panics when `self` is the last representable date.

261.name: succ_opt
261.docs:
Makes a new `Date` for the next date.

Returns `None` when `self` is the last representable date.

262.name: pred
262.docs:
Makes a new `Date` for the prior date.

Panics when `self` is the first representable date.

263.name: pred_opt
263.docs:
Makes a new `Date` for the prior date.

Returns `None` when `self` is the first representable date.

264.name: offset
264.docs: Retrieves an associated offset from UTC.

266.name: with_timezone
266.docs:
Changes the associated time zone.
This does not change the actual `Date` (but will change the string representation).

267.name: checked_add_signed
267.docs:
Adds given `TimeDelta` to the current date.

Returns `None` when it will result in overflow.

268.name: checked_sub_signed
268.docs:
Subtracts given `TimeDelta` from the current date.

Returns `None` when it will result in overflow.

269.name: signed_duration_since
269.docs:
Subtracts another `Date` from the current date.
Returns a `TimeDelta` of integral numbers.

This does not overflow or underflow at all,
as all possible output fits in the range of `TimeDelta`.

270.name: naive_utc
270.docs: Returns a view to the naive UTC date.

271.name: naive_local
271.docs:
Returns a view to the naive local date.

This is technically the same as [`naive_utc`](#method.naive_utc)
because the offset is restricted to never exceed one day,
but provided for the consistency.

272.name: years_since
272.docs: Returns the number of whole years from the given `base` until `self`.

223.name: SubsecRound
223.docs:
Extension trait for subsecond rounding or truncation to a maximum number
of digits. Rounding can be used to decrease the error variance when
serializing/persisting to lower precision. Truncation is the default
behavior in Chrono display formatting.  Either can be used to guarantee
equality (e.g. for testing) when round-tripping through a lower precision
format.

170.name: DateTime
170.docs:
ISO 8601 combined date and time with time zone.

There are some constructors implemented here (the `from_*` methods), but
the general-purpose constructors are all via the methods on the
[`TimeZone`](./offset/trait.TimeZone.html) implementations.

335.name: from_naive_utc_and_offset
335.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from its components: a `NaiveDateTime` in UTC and an `Offset`.

This is a low-level method, intended for use cases such as deserializing a `DateTime` or
passing it through FFI.

336.name: from_utc
336.docs: Makes a new `DateTime` from its components: a `NaiveDateTime` in UTC and an `Offset`.

337.name: from_local
337.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` from a `NaiveDateTime` in *local* time and an `Offset`.

249.name: date
249.docs:
Retrieves the date component with an associated timezone.

Unless you are immediately planning on turning this into a `DateTime`
with the same timezone you should use the [`date_naive`](DateTime::date_naive) method.

342.name: timestamp
342.docs:
Returns the number of non-leap seconds since January 1, 1970 0:00:00 UTC
(aka "UNIX timestamp").

The reverse operation of creating a [`DateTime`] from a timestamp can be performed
using [`from_timestamp`](DateTime::from_timestamp) or [`TimeZone::timestamp_opt`].

343.name: timestamp_millis
343.docs:
Returns the number of non-leap-milliseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

# Example

344.name: timestamp_micros
344.docs:
Returns the number of non-leap-microseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

# Example

345.name: timestamp_nanos
345.docs:

346.name: timestamp_nanos_opt
346.docs:
Returns the number of non-leap-nanoseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

347.name: timestamp_subsec_millis
347.docs:
Returns the number of milliseconds since the last second boundary.

In event of a leap second this may exceed 999.

348.name: timestamp_subsec_micros
348.docs:
Returns the number of microseconds since the last second boundary.

In event of a leap second this may exceed 999,999.

349.name: timestamp_subsec_nanos
349.docs:
Returns the number of nanoseconds since the last second boundary

In event of a leap second this may exceed 999,999,999.

350.name: offset
350.docs: Retrieves an associated offset from UTC.

352.name: with_timezone
352.docs:
Changes the associated time zone.
The returned `DateTime` references the same instant of time from the perspective of the
provided time zone.

353.name: fixed_offset
353.docs:
Fix the offset from UTC to its current value, dropping the associated timezone information.
This is useful for converting a generic `DateTime<Tz: Timezone>` to `DateTime<FixedOffset>`.

354.name: to_utc
354.docs:
Turn this `DateTime` into a `DateTime<Utc>`, dropping the offset and associated timezone
information.

172.name: checked_add_signed
172.docs:
Adds given `TimeDelta` to the current date and time.

356.name: checked_add_months
356.docs:
Adds given `Months` to the current date and time.

Uses the last day of the month if the day does not exist in the resulting month.

178.name: checked_sub_signed
178.docs:
Subtracts given `TimeDelta` from the current date and time.

# Errors

359.name: checked_sub_months
359.docs:
Subtracts given `Months` from the current date and time.

Uses the last day of the month if the day does not exist in the resulting month.

361.name: checked_add_days
361.docs:
Add a duration in [`Days`] to the date part of the `DateTime`.

362.docs:
Subtract a duration in [`Days`] from the date part of the `DateTime`.

363.name: signed_duration_since
363.docs:
Subtracts another `DateTime` from the current date and time.
This does not overflow or underflow at all.

364.docs: Returns a view to the naive UTC datetime.

366.docs:

367.docs:
Set the time to a new fixed time on the existing date.

377.name: from_timestamp_secs
377.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime<Utc>` from the number of non-leap seconds
since January 1, 1970 0:00:00 UTC (aka "UNIX timestamp").

This is a convenience wrapper around [`DateTime::from_timestamp`],
which is useful in functions like [`Iterator::map`] to avoid a closure.

340.name: from_timestamp
340.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime<Utc>` from the number of non-leap seconds
since January 1, 1970 0:00:00 UTC (aka "UNIX timestamp")
and the number of nanoseconds since the last whole non-leap second.

This is guaranteed to round-trip with regard to [`timestamp`](DateTime::timestamp) and
[`timestamp_subsec_nanos`](DateTime::timestamp_subsec_nanos).

374.name: from_timestamp_millis
374.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime<Utc>` from the number of non-leap milliseconds
since January 1, 1970 0:00:00.000 UTC (aka "UNIX timestamp").

This is guaranteed to round-trip with [`timestamp_millis`](DateTime::timestamp_millis).

373.name: from_timestamp_micros
373.docs:
Creates a new `DateTime<Utc>` from the number of non-leap microseconds
since January 1, 1970 0:00:00.000 UTC (aka "UNIX timestamp").

This is guaranteed to round-trip with [`timestamp_micros`](DateTime::timestamp_micros).

375.name: from_timestamp_nanos
375.docs:
Creates a new [`DateTime<Utc>`] from the number of non-leap nanoseconds
since January 1, 1970 0:00:00.000 UTC (aka "UNIX timestamp").

This is guaranteed to round-trip with [`timestamp_nanos`](DateTime::timestamp_nanos).

383.name: parse_from_rfc2822
383.docs:
Parses an RFC 2822 date-and-time string into a `DateTime<FixedOffset>` value.

This parses valid RFC 2822 datetime strings (such as `Tue, 1 Jul 2003 10:52:37 +0200`)
and returns a new [`DateTime`] instance with the parsed timezone as the [`FixedOffset`].

385.name: parse_from_rfc3339
385.docs:
Parses an RFC 3339 date-and-time string into a `DateTime<FixedOffset>` value.

Parses all valid RFC 3339 values (as well as the subset of valid ISO 8601 values that are
also valid RFC 3339 date-and-time values) and returns a new [`DateTime`] with a
[`FixedOffset`] corresponding to the parsed timezone. While RFC 3339 values come in a wide
variety of shapes and sizes, `1996-12-19T16:39:57-08:00` is an example of the most commonly
encountered variety of RFC 3339 formats.

387.name: parse_from_str
387.docs:
Parses a string from a user-specified format into a `DateTime<FixedOffset>` value.

Note that this method *requires a timezone* in the input string. See
[`NaiveDateTime::parse_from_str`](./naive/struct.NaiveDateTime.html#method.parse_from_str)
for a version that does not require a timezone in the to-be-parsed str. The returned
[`DateTime`] value will have a [`FixedOffset`] reflecting the parsed timezone.

389.name: parse_and_remainder
389.docs:
Parses a string from a user-specified format into a `DateTime<FixedOffset>` value, and a
slice with the remaining portion of the string.

Note that this method *requires a timezone* in the input string. See
[`NaiveDateTime::parse_and_remainder`] for a version that does not
require a timezone in `s`. The returned [`DateTime`] value will have a [`FixedOffset`]
reflecting the parsed timezone.

429.name: with_year
429.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the year number changed, while keeping the same month and day.

See also the [`NaiveDate::with_year`] method.

431.name: with_month
431.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the month number (starting from 1) changed.

Don't combine multiple `Datelike::with_*` methods. The intermediate value may not exist.

433.name: with_month0
433.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the month number (starting from 0) changed.

See also the [`NaiveDate::with_month0`] method.

435.name: with_day
435.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the day of month (starting from 1) changed.

See also the [`NaiveDate::with_day`] method.

437.name: with_day0
437.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the day of month (starting from 0) changed.

See also the [`NaiveDate::with_day0`] method.

439.name: with_ordinal
439.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the day of year (starting from 1) changed.

See also the [`NaiveDate::with_ordinal`] method.

441.name: with_ordinal0
441.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the day of year (starting from 0) changed.

See also the [`NaiveDate::with_ordinal0`] method.

448.name: with_hour
448.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the hour number changed.

See also the [`NaiveTime::with_hour`] method.

450.name: with_minute
450.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the minute number changed.

See also the [`NaiveTime::with_minute`] method.

452.name: with_second
452.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with the second number changed.

As with the [`second`](#method.second) method,
the input range is restricted to 0 through 59.

455.name: with_nanosecond
455.docs:
Makes a new `DateTime` with nanoseconds since the whole non-leap second changed.

Returns `None` when the resulting `NaiveDateTime` would be invalid.
As with the [`NaiveDateTime::nanosecond`] method,
the input range can exceed 1,000,000,000 for leap seconds.

226.name: SecondsFormat
226.docs:
Specific formatting options for seconds. This may be extended in the
future, so exhaustive matching in external code is not recommended.

See the `TimeZone::to_rfc3339_opts` function for usage.

228.name: Datelike
228.docs:
The common set of methods for date component.

Methods such as [`year`], [`month`], [`day`] and [`weekday`] can be used to get basic
information about the date.

230.name: Month
230.docs:
The month of the year.

This enum is just a convenience implementation.
The month in dates created by DateLike objects does not return this enum.

1962.name: number_from_month
1962.docs:
Returns a month-of-year number starting from January = 1.

`m`:                     | `January` | `February` | `...` | `December`
-------------------------| --------- | ---------- | --- | -----
`m.number_from_month()`: | 1         | 2          | `...` | 12

1963.name: name
1963.docs: Get the name of the month

1964.name: num_days
1964.docs:
Get the length in days of the month

Yields `None` if `year` is out of range for `NaiveDate`.

2003.name: from_u64
2003.docs:
Returns an `Option<Month>` from a i64, assuming a 1-index, January = 1.

`Month::from_i64(n: i64)`: | `1`                  | `2`                   | ... | `12`
---------------------------| -------------------- | --------------------- | ... | -----
``:                        | Some(Month::January) | Some(Month::February) | ... | Some(Month::December)

232.name: Timelike
232.docs: The common set of methods for time component.

234.name: Weekday
234.docs:
The day of week.

The order of the days of week depends on the context.
(This is why this type does *not* implement `PartialOrd` or `Ord` traits.)
One should prefer `*_from_monday` or `*_from_sunday` methods to get the correct result.

1812.name: pred
1812.docs:
The previous day in the week.

`w`:        | `Mon` | `Tue` | `Wed` | `Thu` | `Fri` | `Sat` | `Sun`
----------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | -----
`w.pred()`: | `Sun` | `Mon` | `Tue` | `Wed` | `Thu` | `Fri` | `Sat`

1813.name: number_from_monday
1813.docs:
Returns a day-of-week number starting from Monday = 1. (ISO 8601 weekday number)

`w`:                      | `Mon` | `Tue` | `Wed` | `Thu` | `Fri` | `Sat` | `Sun`
------------------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | -----
`w.number_from_monday()`: | 1     | 2     | 3     | 4     | 5     | 6     | 7

1814.name: number_from_sunday
1814.docs:
Returns a day-of-week number starting from Sunday = 1.

`w`:                      | `Mon` | `Tue` | `Wed` | `Thu` | `Fri` | `Sat` | `Sun`
------------------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | -----
`w.number_from_sunday()`: | 2     | 3     | 4     | 5     | 6     | 7     | 1

1815.name: num_days_from_monday
1815.docs:
Returns a day-of-week number starting from Monday = 0.

`w`:                        | `Mon` | `Tue` | `Wed` | `Thu` | `Fri` | `Sat` | `Sun`
--------------------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | -----
`w.num_days_from_monday()`: | 0     | 1     | 2     | 3     | 4     | 5     | 6

1816.name: num_days_from_sunday
1816.docs:
Returns a day-of-week number starting from Sunday = 0.

`w`:                        | `Mon` | `Tue` | `Wed` | `Thu` | `Fri` | `Sat` | `Sun`
--------------------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | -----
`w.num_days_from_sunday()`: | 1     | 2     | 3     | 4     | 5     | 6     | 0

1817.name: days_since
1817.docs:
The number of days since the given day.

# Examples

1857.docs:
Any weekday can be represented as an integer from 0 to 6, which equals to
[`Weekday::num_days_from_monday`](#method.num_days_from_monday) in this implementation.
Do not heavily depend on this though; use explicit methods whenever possible.

236.name: FixedOffset
236.docs:
The time zone with fixed offset, from UTC-23:59:59 to UTC+23:59:59.

Using the [`TimeZone`](./trait.TimeZone.html) methods
on a `FixedOffset` struct is the preferred way to construct
`DateTime<FixedOffset>` instances. See the [`east_opt`](#method.east_opt) and
[`west_opt`](#method.west_opt) methods for examples.

1614.name: east
1614.docs:
Makes a new `FixedOffset` for the Eastern Hemisphere with given timezone difference.
The negative `secs` means the Western Hemisphere.

Panics on the out-of-bound `secs`.

1615.name: east_opt
1615.docs:
Makes a new `FixedOffset` for the Eastern Hemisphere with given timezone difference.
The negative `secs` means the Western Hemisphere.

Returns `None` on the out-of-bound `secs`.

1616.name: west
1616.docs:
Makes a new `FixedOffset` for the Western Hemisphere with given timezone difference.
The negative `secs` means the Eastern Hemisphere.

Panics on the out-of-bound `secs`.

1617.name: west_opt
1617.docs:
Makes a new `FixedOffset` for the Western Hemisphere with given timezone difference.
The negative `secs` means the Eastern Hemisphere.

Returns `None` on the out-of-bound `secs`.

1618.name: local_minus_utc
1618.docs: Returns the number of seconds to add to convert from UTC to the local time.

1619.name: utc_minus_local
1619.docs: Returns the number of seconds to add to convert from the local time to UTC.

238.name: Utc
238.docs:
The UTC time zone. This is the most efficient time zone when you don't need the local time.
It is also used as an offset (which is also a dummy type).

Using the [`TimeZone`](./trait.TimeZone.html) methods
on the UTC struct is the preferred way to construct `DateTime<Utc>`
instances.

183.name: NaiveDate
183.docs:
ISO 8601 calendar date without timezone.
Allows for every [proleptic Gregorian date] from Jan 1, 262145 BCE to Dec 31, 262143 CE.
Also supports the conversion from ISO 8601 ordinal and week date.

# Calendar Date

The calculation to go from a local time (wall clock time) to an instant in UTC can end up in
three cases:
* A single, simple result.
* An ambiguous result when the clock is turned backwards during a transition due to for example
  DST.
* No result when the clock is turned forwards during a transition due to for example DST.

Extension trait for rounding or truncating a DateTime by a TimeDelta.

Both rounding and truncating are done via [`TimeDelta::num_nanoseconds`] and
[`DateTime::timestamp_nanos_opt`]. This means that they will fail if either the
`TimeDelta` or the `DateTime` are too big to represented as nanoseconds. They
will also fail if the `TimeDelta` is bigger than the timestamp, negative or zero.
